title: Booleans
learningObjectives: Explain booleans and write predictable JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: The boolean type has two values: true and false. Boolean values commonly represent conditions, state, and the results of comparison or logical operations. JavaScript also has truthy and falsy values that can be converted to booleans in conditional contexts.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit boolean state makes conditions easier to understand. Avoid confusing a boolean with strings such as 'true' or numbers such as 1, even though some values are truthy.
understand.analogy: A boolean is a yes/no value used to represent whether a condition is satisfied.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript values, scope, and runtime behaviour follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: The condition is true because access is granted and completion is false.

examples.explanation: The condition is true because access is granted and completion is false.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page or developer console shows the values and behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Create three boolean variables for a learning dashboard and use them in if statements. Compare true with the string 'true'.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program that uses the concept in a realistic learning-app example. Inspect values and errors in the console.
hints: Prefer const unless reassignment is required.
Do not expose private data in console output.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Booleans</title></head><body>
<script>const hasAccess=true;const isComplete=false;if(hasAccess&&!isComplete){console.log('Continue the lesson');}</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: How many primitive values does the boolean type have?
questions.explanation: The boolean type has true and false.

questions.prompt: What should a learner do when a JavaScript value behaves unexpectedly?
options: Assume every variable has a fixed type
questions.explanation: Inspecting type and value helps identify unexpected coercion or operations.
